estimates.claim: The UN Group puts coltan smuggled each month from Rubaya to Rwanda at about 150 t, which it says is larger than any earlier traceability breach.
The Group says at least 150 t of coltan were fraudulently exported to Rwanda and mixed with Rwandan production.
The Group's 2024 estimate is about 120 t a month of Rubaya coltan traded and transported under M23 control; Global Witness describes this as trafficked to Rwanda.
estimates.paragraph_or_page: S/2026/466 para 213, citing S/2024/969 para 64; GW web page

estimates.claim: The MONUSCO head (SRSG Keita) gave a conservative estimate of 100 t of coltan produced in Rubaya each month, as cited by the Group.
A 3D satellite model of Rubaya (March 2026) showed much more mining activity than a year earlier. The Group assesses output above the 2024 level of about 120 t a month, without giving a new figure.
Nine RDF-type trucks and three vehicles carrying Rubaya minerals crossed the Grande Barrière into Rwanda in one week. At the Group's payload estimates that is about 195 t.
M23 looted more than 500 t of tagged and untagged 3T from exporters' warehouses in Goma and Bukavu. In Rwanda, looted minerals were mixed with local production.
estimates.what_it_measures: looted volume (DRC exporters' stock, partly laundered via Rwanda)

estimates.claim: M23 looted 186 t of untagged 3T at Nyabibwe (South Kivu) and smuggled it to Rwanda through Mukwija port (Kalehe).
Global Witness says at least 1,400 t of coltan, and probably much more, was smuggled from DRC to Rwanda in the first year after M23 took Rubaya.
Customs records show Kanzamin Ltd, a Rwandan exporter the Group links to the Rubaya chain, exported at least 70 t of coltan.
estimates.what_it_measures: exporter volume linked to M23 supply chain

estimates.claim: Rwanda's cassiterite exports rose 58%, from 4,859 t to 7,700 t (NBR data). The Group says the rise matches M23-area smuggling in timing and size.
The rise of about 2,841 t was slightly more than South Kivu's officially recorded 2024 cassiterite production. It also coincided with the end of official state exports from Bukavu in Feb 2025.

Rwanda's largest cassiterite miner and its only tin refinery made about 60% of 2024 cassiterite exports and did not increase in 2025. Domestic output alone would need the smaller producers to triple, and the Group found no development to explain that.

Rwanda's coltan exports followed the same upward trend as cassiterite, less steeply. From Q2 2025, Rwandan coltan and cassiterite exports rose sharply, which domestic production does not support and which tracks output in M23 areas.
Large volumes of 3T from the main M23-controlled areas of North and South Kivu were diverted to Rwanda.
About half of South Kivu's cassiterite and coltan production now comes from M23-held territory (after Nzibira fell on 21 Sep 2025).
estimates.what_it_measures: share of supply area under M23 control

estimates.claim: More than two thirds of South Kivu's wolframite output comes from M23-held territory.
estimates.what_it_measures: share of supply area under M23 control

estimates.claim: South Kivu produced about 3,000 t of cassiterite and 200 t of wolframite in 2024 (DRC Ministry of Mines), about 20% and 60% of national artisanal exports.
About 40 t a month (about 480 t a year) of cassiterite and wolframite passed through the Nzibira hub before M23 took it.

Rwanda's coltan exports rose 50% in 2023, an increase the Group called unprecedented. At least part of Rubaya output was smuggled across the border; Rubaya trade then ran through M23-controlled routes, while production was under PARECO-FF/Wazalendo.
Information obtained by the Group shows that not all coltan Rwanda exported in 2024 could have come from domestic production.
The RDB's claimed domestic output of 8,000-9,000 t of 3T a year is contradicted by NISR data, independent geology and ITSCI records, according to the Group.
Regional geology (BGR) puts coltan at a mean 25% of mixed coltan-cassiterite deposits. The RDB's claims imply 60-70% in Rwanda.
estimates.unit: % mean coltan share in mixed deposits
estimates.what_it_measures: geological plausibility of RWA coltan output

estimates.claim: ITSCI opened 51 incident inquiries in Rwanda over plausibility or misrepresented mineral origin.
NBR coltan exports were 1,046 t (2021), 1,305 t (2022), 2,070 t (2023) and 2,384 t (2024). They were more than 2.5 times the 2021 level by 2025.
Other countries reported over 2,900 t of coltan imports from Rwanda in 2024, more than Rwanda's official exports. GW says some coltan may have left Rwanda unrecorded.
Tantalite's share of ITSCI-tagged 3T exports rose from 21% to 31%. Global Witness says this is hard to explain without Rubaya smuggling.
A former Pact manager estimated only about 10% of minerals Rwanda exported were mined there. In his view that stayed true even as domestic output grew, because smuggling also grew.
estimates.unit: % of RWA 3T exports of Rwandan origin (implies ~90% DRC)

estimates.claim: Two industry sources told GW they had warned Apple, Intel and others that smuggled minerals made up to 90% of Rwanda's exports.
ITSCI recorded 2,038 t of Rwandan tantalum exports (-13%), while world imports from Rwanda were 3,264 t (+12%), a gap of 1,226 t.
estimates.what_it_measures: gap between ITSCI-traced and total RWA tantalum trade

estimates.claim: ITSCI recorded 2,354 t (+14%) of Rwandan tantalum exports, while world imports from Rwanda were 2,909 t (+51%, +980 t).
NBR 3T exports reached 13,295 t (+33%, +3,308 t), while ITSCI-recorded exports fell to 6,646 t (-11%). ITSCI covered about 50% of official exports.
ITSCI-recorded Rwandan cassiterite exports were 3,326 t (-6%), far below the 7,700 t NBR figure the UN quotes.
NBR tantalum exports rose 9% (+212 t) and trade data 12% (+355 t), while ITSCI-recorded exports fell 13% (-316 t).
estimates.what_it_measures: Rwanda export growth vs traced supply

estimates.claim: NBR tungsten exports rose 10% (+268 t) while ITSCI-recorded exports fell 18% (-273 t). ITSCI accounts for less than 50% of Rwandan tungsten exports.
estimates.what_it_measures: Rwanda export growth vs traced supply

estimates.claim: Rubaya mines supply about 15% of global tantalum, according to Global Witness. Reuters says 15% of the world's coltan. No UN paragraph was found for this figure.
A Reuters analysis of customs records says Boss Mining exported at least 150 t of coltan ($6.6m, 6.5% of Rwanda's coltan exports).
estimates.what_it_measures: exporter volume linked to M23 supply chain

estimates.claim: An academic working paper finds a 150% rise in Rwandan coltan exports after the EACRF withdrawal and systematic gaps between declared production and exports.
Rwanda's prime minister reported over 19 t of gold exports for 2024. USGS puts domestic production at 2.9 t (end 2022). GI-TOC says that, even counting declared imports, about 3.1 t is unexplained.

About 13 t of gold imports into Rwanda were declared from Burkina Faso, Cameroon, CAR, Kenya, Tanzania, South Africa and the UAE. None were declared from DRC, although smuggling from DRC is long documented.
estimates.what_it_measures: declared non-DRC origin of RWA gold

estimates.claim: Bukavu trade sources say DRC gold still moves through Rwanda and that after M23 took Bukavu the trade was 'somehow formalized'.
OFAC says RDF and M23 moved at least 60 kg of gold from RDF/M23-held South Kivu areas via Rusizi to Gasabo Gold Refinery in Kigali.
Rwanda exported a record $885m of gold in 2023 despite having no major domestic gold mines. DRC's artisanal gold, over $1bn a year, is almost all smuggled, mainly to Rwanda and Uganda.
Over $4bn a year of conflict-affected or high-risk gold from Central and East Africa reaches world markets, much of it via neighbours including Rwanda.
Uganda exported about 62 t of gold ($6.4bn, +30%). The Group attributes the surge largely to DRC gold, especially from Djugu (Ituri). This shows a major DRC gold outlet that is not Rwanda.
DRC-Rwanda tensions disrupted the Rwanda gold-smuggling route, and smugglers, including those linked to armed groups in Uvira and Fizi, increasingly diverted gold to Burundi.
It is highly likely that gold needing refining was brought to Gasabo Gold Refinery. The Group asked Rwanda to make Gasabo ascertain gold origin.

alternative_explanations.claim: Rwanda produces 8,000-9,000 t of 3T a year and more than 22% of world tantalum, so exports are domestic. (S/2025/446 para 120 says this is contradicted by NISR data, geology and ITSCI records.)
Rwanda's gold refinery, tantalum refinery and tin smelter can process minerals 'from within the country and the region'. Rwanda presents regional processing as legitimate.
Export growth from $373m (2017) to $1.75bn (2024) comes from value addition, diversified markets, professional mining, mechanisation, exploration and investment.
alternative_explanations.by_whom: Rwanda Mines, Petroleum and Gas Board

alternative_explanations.claim: Rwanda does not depend on DRC; 'our own hills have minerals'. The aim is to be a regional trading hub for processed minerals.
Processing minerals 'from anywhere' should not be a problem. Developed economies profit from minerals they do not mine. Minerals from Katanga and Equateur use other routes.
Congolese gold and coltan pass through Rwanda as a transit corridor to Mombasa and Dar es Salaam; this is trade, not smuggling or laundering.

Non-ITSCI operators and other traceability systems explain part of the rise, so ITSCI data cover only about 50% of official 3T exports. A non-ITSCI tin smelter in Rwanda reports a 74% rise in metal output from 2023 to 2025, which ITSCI assumes is in the NBR figures. This explains where the extra volume is recorded, not where the ore comes from.

Fraud risk includes 'internal fraud of domestic mined production within Rwanda' as well as cross-border fraud. ITSCI supports District Mining Task Forces on informal Rwandan mining. Informal, unrecorded Rwandan mining is therefore a possible source of part of the gap.

Trade-database figures may include warehousing, are prone to misclassification, and one country corrected a 2025 month after ITSCI queried it. Year-on-year swings of 20-30% are normal (price, licences).

Gold imports into Rwanda are declared from Burkina Faso, Cameroon, CAR, Kenya, Tanzania, South Africa and the UAE (about 13 t in part of 2024). GI-TOC notes DRC is not declared even though smuggling from DRC is documented.

South Kivu coltan was smuggled to Rwanda BEFORE M23 entered South Kivu (Mwenga, Shabunda, Kalehe, Idjwi). Drivers include a 34-step, 61-signature export process, armed groups at sites, and corrupt state agents and FARDC. Part of the gap is therefore DRC material from areas not controlled by M23, though not necessarily free of armed groups.
alternative_explanations.by_whom: IPIS Voix du Congo (anonymous civil-society author)

alternative_explanations.claim: Part of what M23 moved to Rwanda in 2025 was stock looted from legitimate Congolese exporters (over 500 t, some of it ITSCI-tagged), not newly mined ore from M23 sites.

Before 30 Apr 2024, Rubaya production was under PARECO-FF control, and trade was split among PARECO-FF, Wazalendo and M23. Pre-2024 Rubaya-origin material in Rwandan exports cannot all be attributed to M23.
alternative_explanations.by_whom: UN Group of Experts (via ReliefWeb summary)

alternative_explanations.claim: A large share of DRC gold goes to Uganda (Ituri/Djugu, about 62 t of Ugandan exports in 2025) and Burundi (Uvira/Fizi, 2023), not Rwanda.

Burundi as an overland origin of Rwandan exports is constrained: Burundi closed its land border with Rwanda in Jan 2024. Whether it was still closed in 2026 is confirmed only by a non-authoritative travel page.
alternative_explanations.by_whom: Government of Rwanda (statement on the closure)

alternative_explanations.claim: Recycling, scrap or stockpile drawdown as an explanation for 3T or gold exports: NO source found on record from Rwanda, ITSCI, the UN or NGOs. Treat as an unexamined gap.
Uganda or Burundi 3T ore entering Rwanda for export (2024-2026): NO source found. Burundi has 3T deposits (EAC profile, search snippet only), but no document shows the flow.

denials.respondent: Government of Rwanda (spokesperson Yolande Makolo, to Reuters)
denials.summary: Makolo said the UN Group's report misrepresents Rwanda's long-standing security concerns about Hutu rebel groups, which she said require a defensive posture on the border. Reuters notes that Rwanda has long denied trafficking coltan looted from DRC or backing M23.

In a letter to the Security Council President, Rwanda opposed creating an ICGLR ad hoc commission of inquiry into alleged mineral smuggling to Rwanda. It repeated this at the ICGLR mines ministers' meeting on 31 Jul 2025, but the commission was set up on 3 Aug 2025. The letter is known only through the Group's account; annexes 42-43 were not read.

denials.respondent: Government of Rwanda (President Kagame; RMB CEO Alice Uwase)
denials.summary: Both dismissed concerns that Rwanda processes Congolese minerals. Uwase said Rwanda does not depend on DRC; Kagame said processing minerals from anywhere should not be a problem. This is not a specific denial of M23-linked sourcing.
On 2 Apr 2026 the Group asked Rwanda to explain the reported origins of its increased cassiterite and coltan exports. No reply had arrived when the report was published.

denials.respondent: Rwanda Mines, Petroleum and Gas Board (non-response); Halcyon (denial)
denials.summary: RMB did not answer Global Witness's questions about seizures of smuggled coltan. Halcyon confirmed buying from Kanzamin but denied the coltan came from Rubaya.
Amnesty wrote to RMB on 6 Aug 2026 and President Kagame on 17 Aug 2026 about mineral trafficking to Rwanda. No response by publication.
Balinda accepted that DRC gold and coltan pass through Rwanda but denied this is smuggling or laundering.

UNVERIFIED (search snippet only): ITSCI's response to 'The ITSCI laundromat' rejects the claim that up to 90% of Rwanda's exported minerals were not produced there. It calls GW's sources unreliable and says GW ignored mixed production.
